content.body:
The Hurricane IIb, the "12 gun shotgun," was almost identical to the Hurricane IIc except in armament. It employed four more .303 machineguns than its earlier variation, the venerable Hurricane I. Since the anticipated Hispano 20 mm cannons had experienced problems and delays in equipping the RAF's aircraft, some form of firepower upgrade was needed. It also had increased horsepower from its Merlin XX engine, which gave it a handy increase in speed and climb ability over the earlier Hurricane I.
Contributing to its fighting ability was its somewhat legendary durability as a result of the old fashioned wooden stringer fuselage construction, which by this stage of the war made it rather unique. Still, it is not very fast, but pilots who love the idea of TWELVE machineguns for some shotgun-like bullet coverage may grow to love their Hurricane IIb's.
content.brief: TYPE: Fighter Interceptor MAX. SPEED: 530 km/h WEIGHT: 2,990 kg CREW: 1 ARMAMENT: .303 cal Browning LMGs (12)
content.title: Hawker Hurricane IIb
